events.title: Morris worm spreads on the internet
events.summary: The Morris worm began spreading on November 2, 1988 — the first worm to gain mainstream attention, infecting thousands of Unix systems on the early internet.
events.about: Robert Tappan Morris's worm exploited sendmail, finger, and rsh flaws — clogging networks when it re-infected machines too aggressively. The incident created the CERT coordination center, hardened Unix admin practices, and the first felony conviction under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act.

narrative.whyChosen: The Morris worm was the internet's first major security wake-up call.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved connected computers needed incident response and patch discipline.
narrative.problemSolved: Nothing yet — it exposed that the growing internet had no coordinated defense against self-replicating code.
